name: Sunlight Zone
summary: The upper ocean where photosynthesis can occur and most familiar marine food webs begin.
conditions: Strongest daily and seasonal temperature changes
Highest direct connection to weather and atmosphere

name: Twilight Zone
light: Fading sunlight; too little for photosynthesis
summary: A dim global layer where enormous numbers of animals migrate upward at night and descend before dawn.
conditions: Diel vertical migration moves animals and carbon

name: Midnight Zone
temperature: Near 4°C in much of the open ocean
summary: The largest continuously dark habitat, where food is scarce and animals rely on specialized senses, lures and low-energy strategies.
conditions: Sparse food delivered from above or captured from other animals

name: Abyssal Zone
summary: A vast, cold region above the deep seafloor, supplied mainly by organic material sinking from shallower water.
conditions: Very limited food except around special habitats

name: Hadal Zone
summary: The trench zone: narrow, extremely deep habitats with specialized communities and the ocean’s highest pressures.
conditions: Food can collect along trench floors and slopes
